title: PPE Inspection Checklist (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.132)
subtitle: For supervisors checking PPE paperwork, condition, fit, training and payment on site.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
Where an item is marked Defect, do not use defective or damaged PPE (1910.132(e)) and correct the item.
Each item cites the 1910.132 paragraph it checks.

sections.title: Hazard assessment and certification
items: The employer has assessed this workplace to determine whether hazards needing PPE are present or likely to be present.
The written certification identifies the workplace that was evaluated.
The certification names the person who certifies the evaluation was performed.
The date or dates the assessment was carried out appear on the certification.
The document states that it is a certification of hazard assessment.
The PPE types selected protect against the hazards the assessment identified.
Workers asked on site can say which PPE was selected for their task.

sections.title: PPE use and condition
items: Every worker on a task covered by the assessment is wearing the selected PPE types.
Each worker's PPE fits that worker properly.
Protective equipment is kept in a sanitary and reliable condition.
Protective shields and barriers needed for the hazard are in place and intact.
No item in use is cracked, torn, holed, missing parts or otherwise damaged; damaged items are taken out of service.
PPE in use is of safe design and construction for the job being done.
Any PPE workers supply themselves has been confirmed adequate, maintained and sanitary.

sections.title: Training and retraining
items: Each worker required to use PPE has been trained.
Workers can say when PPE is required for their tasks.
Workers can name the PPE required for their tasks.
Workers put on, adjust, wear and take off their PPE correctly when observed.
Workers can describe the limitations of their PPE.
Workers know how to care for and maintain their PPE, its useful life and how to dispose of it.
Each worker has demonstrated understanding of the training and the ability to use PPE properly before starting work that requires PPE.
Workers whose previous training was made obsolete by workplace changes or by changes in PPE types have been retrained.
Workers seen misusing assigned PPE or lacking knowledge of it have been retrained.

sections.title: PPE payment
items: Workers have not been charged for required PPE outside the listed exceptions.
Replacement PPE is provided at no cost unless the worker lost it or damaged it on purpose.
Workers not made to buy PPE
No worker is required to provide or pay for their own PPE beyond the excepted items.
Where workers pay for non-specialty safety-toe footwear or non-specialty prescription safety eyewear, they may wear it off the job site.

references: 29 CFR 1910.132: General requirements (Part 1910 Subpart I, Personal Protective Equipment)
